messages:
Maria P.: Did an ephemeral-CA dry run in eu-west at ~10:15 UTC; seeing intermittent TLS handshake failures for services behind gw-proxy.
A.Johnson: When did you run it?
Maria P.: 10:15 UTC. Repro with curl loop — logs below.
Ryan T.: paste the curl + output pls
Maria P.: ```for i in {1..20}; do curl -v --resolve api.redwood-eu:443:34.89.10.11 https://api.redwood-eu/health || true; done
* Connected to api.redwood-eu (34.89.10.11) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1): no shared cipher
* SSL: Handshake failed
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:tls13_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure```
Olivia L.: "no shared cipher" -> likely cipher policy mismatch after the CA swap. Did the rotator issue a different curve or signature alg?
Maria P.: Chain shows ECDSA P-384; some proxies expect RSA or ECDSA P-256 for legacy backends.
sec-bot: [alert] canaries failing (ephemeral-ca-dryrun) — 17% handshake fail rate in eu-west
A.Johnson: We rolled an RBAC change earlier that tightened keystore principal mapping for rotator; might've changed the key template used for leaf issuance.
Ryan T.: Check keystore metadata: `keystorectl describe rotator/issuer`
Maria P.: Output:
$ keystorectl describe rotator/issuer
issuer: rotator-v2
signer: cloud-kms:projects/rr-keys/locations/eu-west/keyR
algo: ECDSA_P384
validity: 12h

Olivia L.: There it is — rotator-v2 is using P-384. Our proxy cipher config allowed only P-256 and RSA due to legacy perf constraints.
A.Johnson: Remediation plan: 1) Short-term: add P-384 to gw-proxy cipherlist on eu-west canary hosts and restart; 2) Medium: update rotator key-template to issue P-256 for legacy services while retaining P-384 for new workloads; 3) Add an audit marker for issuer/key-template changes.
Maria P.: I'll patch 3 canary hosts now. Any objections?
Ryan T.: No objections. Also add an audit rule to flag issuer.algo != expected.
Olivia L.: I'll open a quick runbook entry documenting the RBAC->keystore coupling, including `keystorectl` diff checks and expected issuer metadata.
Maria P.: Patch command used:
# on gateway canary host
sudo sed -i 's/P-256/P-256,P-384/' /etc/gw-proxy/cipher-policy.conf
sudo systemctl restart gw-proxy
oncall-bot: paging oncall: security-team oncall (p1) — canary patch in progress
sec-bot: [audit] RBAC change detected: service=rotator actor=ajohnson action=update_issuer key=rotator-v2 at=2025-05-12T10:05:12Z
Maria P.: Results: patched hosts 20/20 curl health OK; unpatched hosts still ~3/20 fails.
Ryan T.: Next steps: add unit test in rotator CI asserting `issuer.algo in allowed_algos` per environment; add an admission webhook eval in keystore flow.
Olivia L.: Audit rule: detect issuer.algo drift -> route to `security-audit` topic and link runbook.
Maria P.: Filing follow-ups: 1) rollback path if cipherlist revert needed; 2) keystore template change plan; 3) audit rule + webhook test. Tagging vuln-triage since handshake surface area was affected.
Maria P.: Closing canary thread — will update incident document with timestamps and logs.
sec-bot: [info] incident-tagged: "ephemeral-ca-keystore-algo-drift" severity=low-moderate
